corpus.notes: A dense, very recent P1 sweep (issues #204-#217, dated 2026-08-02, plus #175-#196 from 2026-07-07/18) already covers nearly every hot path through v0.0.19: display-list O(N^2) build (#175), selector backtracking (#179), cascade O(elements x rules) (#21) + per-decl churn (#178) + SiblingRef (#26), layout re-run/clone-per-frame (#22/#207), mirror re-cascade per window (#215), JS budget gaps (#213), per-event DOM serialize+restyle (#195), unbounded hinter map (#205) + glyph re-outline (#38), image sync decode (#211), no transport reuse (#210), DNS single-flight (#184), header-count cap (#186), body copy (#180), cookie/storage/SVG unbounded collections (#176/#182/#194), Storage global dirty flag (#217), framebuffer per-pixel blit (#214). Intervening review-state PRs (#154-#197) were closed as no-ops by the owner, so STATE.json had not advanced past the 2026-07-01 record. This run re-based on the current corpus and targeted genuine gaps only.

findings.title: HttpCache never evicts expired entries and has no count/byte cap — stale entries pin response bodies via strong Arc, so cache memory grows monotonically per session
findings.rationale: Distinct from #25 (Weak intern-pool pruning on clear_instance), #24 (clone-on-get) and #173 (navigation-only coverage): the entries map itself has no expiry eviction and no cap, and Entry.body is a strong Arc, so expired-but-retained entries pin bodies for the instance lifetime. Confirmed store() is the only growth path and is navigation-only; only removal is whole-instance clear_instance.

overall_health: Good and actively hardening. The browser has had two heavy, well-executed performance passes (v0.0.15-v0.0.19 in-tree work plus the 2026-08-02 review filing #204-#217), and the open P1 backlog is thorough and specific rather than stale. This run found the field already densely covered and deliberately did not pad: a single genuinely novel, code-confirmed P1 finding (#221, HttpCache lacks expiry-eviction and a cap, pinning response bodies via strong Arc — distinct from the #25 Weak-pool leak) plus reconciliation confirming the recent-change surface (table cap, viewport cull, z-index, glyph/hinter caches, mirror path) is either correct or already tracked. Highest-value open items to prioritize next remain the O(N^2)/exponential algorithmic ones (#175 display-list build, #170 nested flex/grid, #179 selector backtracking) and the unbounded-collection family (#176/#182/#194/#205/#221).
